title: Automorphisms of a rank-one finite locally constant sheaf
statement:
In the purity conventions of this chapter ([def-pur-conventions] finite setting $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n\mathcal O_E$ of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]),
let $T$ be a separated [def-weil-proper-morphism]
finite-type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] $k$-scheme and let $L,M$ be finite locally constant
$\Lambda$-sheaves of rank one on $T$ [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf]. Here rank one means locally isomorphic to the coefficient module sheaf $\Lambda_T$ on a covering of the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; restrictions are those of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Hom is ordinary sheaf Hom [def-pur-sheaf-hom], and geometric stalks are those of [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk]. The integral and rational coefficient transports in the conventions are separate from this ordinary finite-sheaf assertion.

1. The canonical map $\Lambda_T\to\mathcal Hom(L,L)$,
$1\mapsto\operatorname{id}_L$, is an isomorphism; hence every
endomorphism of $L$ is multiplication by a unique locally
constant function $T\to\Lambda$, and
$\operatorname{Aut}(L)=\Gamma(T,\Lambda_T^\times)$ is the group
of locally constant units.
1. Any two isomorphisms $\varphi,\psi:L\to M$ differ by a unique
automorphism of $M$: there is a unique locally constant unit
$u\in\Gamma(T,\Lambda_T^\times)$ with $\psi=u\cdot\varphi$.
In particular, given an isomorphism $\varphi:L\to M$, for every geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$ and
every unit $v\in\Lambda^\times$ there is an isomorphism
$\psi:L\to M$ with $\psi_{\bar t}=v\cdot\varphi_{\bar t}$,
namely $\psi=v\cdot\varphi$ for the constant unit $v$.

proof.text: By clause (4) of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ is a finite commutative ring, so the finite-ring comparison used below applies. Put $R=\Lambda_T$. The locally constant rank-one hypothesis, with the local-constancy meaning of [def-weil-proetale-locally-constant-sheaf], gives a covering $\{U_i\to T\}$ and $R|_{U_i}$-linear isomorphisms $e_i:L|_{U_i}\simeq R|_{U_i}$. Define $a:R\to\mathcal Hom_R(L,L)$ by $a_V(r)(s)=rs$ on every localization. It is a map of $R$-modules because $R$ is commutative, and it sends $1$ to the identity. This construction is independent of the chosen $e_i$.

source.place: Proof Step 1: rank-one trivializing cover and canonical scalar map

proof.text: On $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/U_i$, ordinary Hom commutes with restriction directly from [def-pur-sheaf-hom]: its value at $V/U_i$ is the Hom of the restrictions to $T_{\mathrm{proet}}/V$, identified sectionwise by the relocalization rule of [def-pur-localized-ringed-site]. Conjugate by the restriction of $e_i$ to reduce $a_V$ to the scalar map $R(V)\to\operatorname{End}_{R|_V}(R|_V)$. For an $R|_V$-linear sheaf endomorphism $h$, put $b=h_V(1)\in R(V)$. For every $W\to V$ and $x\in R(W)$, naturality and linearity give $h_W(x)=x h_W(1)=x\,b|_W$. Thus $h$ is multiplication by $b$. Conversely multiplication by any $b$ is a linear sheaf map and its value on $1$ at $V$ is $b$. These two identities prove that evaluation at $1$ and scalar multiplication are inverse. For $V'\to V$, the scalar of $h|_{V'}$ is $h_{V'}(1)=b|_{V'}$, so the inverses commute with every further restriction. This proves $a|_{U_i}$ is an isomorphism without a constant-module comparison or a finite-presentation theorem.

source.place: Proof Step 1 local free rank-one computation, expanded by evaluation at 1; ordinary Hom restriction is Stacks sites-modules.tex Tag 0E8H (lemma-internal-hom-restriction), immediate from the definitions

proof.text: Here is the sheaf argument passing from the local inverses to a global inverse. For any object $V$ and $h\in\mathcal Hom_R(L,L)(V)$, pull back the cover to $V_i=V\times_TU_i$. Each $h|_{V_i}$ has a unique preimage $r_i\in R(V_i)$ under $a$. On $V_i\times_VV_j$ the two $r_i$ restrict to the same element because their images are both the restriction of $h$ and $a$ is injective there by step 2. The equalizer sheaf axiom of [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] glues them to a unique $r\in R(V)$; separatedness gives $a(r)=h$. The same argument proves injectivity. Restricting this unique preimage to $W\to V$ gives the unique preimage of $h|_W$, so the inverses are natural and $R$-linear. This proves $a$ is an isomorphism of sheaves.

source.place: Proof Step 1: sheaf descent of the local isomorphisms, written sectionwise

proof.text:
To justify the words locally constant function on the underlying scheme, write $C=\underline\Lambda$ on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$ and $D=R$ on $T_{\mathrm{proet}}$. In this step all Hom sets are in sheaves of modules over the fixed ring $\Lambda$, using the underlying $\Lambda$-module sheaves of $C$ and $D$. The comparison adjunction of [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism] gives, for every pro-etale $\Lambda$-module sheaf $F$, natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}(
u_T^*C,F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(C,
u_{T,*}F)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_\Lambda(\Lambda,F(T))\cong\operatorname{Hom}(D,F).$$
For the middle and last bijections, [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] and the constant-module construction of [def-sf-site-constant-module-functor] say that a map from the constant sheaf is exactly a map from the constant presheaf. Such a natural map is determined by its component at the final object $T$, with all other components its restrictions, and $(
u_{T,*}F)(T)=F(T)$ by the comparison's displayed definition. Write $X=
u_T^*C$ and let $\Theta_F:\operatorname{Hom}(X,F)\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Hom}(D,F)$ be this natural bijection. Set $b=\Theta_X(1_X):D	o X$ and $c=\Theta_D^{-1}(1_D):X	o D$. Naturality under postcomposition by $c$ gives $c\circ b=\Theta_D(c)=1_D$. Naturality under postcomposition by $b$ gives $\Theta_X(b\circ c)=b\circ\Theta_D(c)=b=\Theta_X(1_X)$; injectivity of $\Theta_X$ gives $b\circ c=1_X$. Thus $c$ is the required isomorphism $
u_T^*C\simeq D$. To check the constant labels used below, let $\eta:C	o
u_{T,*}X$ be the adjunction unit. Under the displayed Hom bijections, $\Theta_D(c)=1_D$ says precisely that the adjunct $
u_{T,*}c\circ\eta:C	o
u_{T,*}D$ sends the section labelled $1$ at $T$ to the section labelled $1$ in $D(T)$. Its $\Lambda$-linearity therefore sends every constant label $r\in\Lambda$ to $r$, and naturality gives the same assertion on every etale object $V	o T$ by restriction from $T$. Thus the composite of the unit with $
u_{T,*}c$, which is exactly the comparison used in step 5, preserves constant labels and restrictions. This is the constant-coefficient identification needed below.

source.place: Proof Step 1: expanded constant-coefficient comparison by adjunction and sheafification, before the global-function interpretation

proof.text: The unit isomorphism $C\to\nu_{T,*}\nu_T^*C$ from [prop-weil-pbc-site-comparison-finite-level], evaluated at $T$ and followed by the isomorphism of step 4, identifies $C(T)$ with $R(T)$. Its finite-ring hypothesis holds because $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$ in [def-pur-conventions] is finite by clause (4) of [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], as noted in step 1. The natural model [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-locally-constant], applied to the $\Lambda$-module $\Lambda$, identifies $C(T)$ with $\operatorname{LC}(|T|,\Lambda)$. It imposes no connectedness or nonemptiness hypothesis. More precisely, choose the constant-label model as follows. That lemma implies the presheaf of locally constant maps is a sheaf. The map from the constant presheaf sends $r$ to the constant function $r$. It is locally surjective by restriction to the open fibers of any locally constant function, an etale covering by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-etale] and [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. It is locally injective: equal constant functions have equal labels on a nonempty object, while the empty covering handles the empty object. By [lem-weil-pbc-site-sheafification-iso-locally-bijective] this map induces an isomorphism from the constant sheaf to the locally constant model. Thus the identifications preserve constant sections and restrictions. They also preserve addition and multiplication: after restricting a section of $C$ to the open fibers of its locally constant model, it is a constant section; products of two sections are checked on the intersections of these open fibers, where the assertion is the equality of their labels' product in $\Lambda$. Explicitly, let $\beta_V:C(V)\to R(V)$ be the comparison on an etale object $V$. If $s,t\in C(T)$ have respective labels $a,b$ on the intersection $W$ of two open fibers, then naturality and preservation of constant sections give $\beta_T(st)|_W=\beta_W(ab)=ab=\beta_T(s)|_W\,\beta_T(t)|_W$. These intersections cover $T$, so the sheaf uniqueness axiom gives $\beta_T(st)=\beta_T(s)\beta_T(t)$ globally; the constant label $1$ gives preservation of the identity. Thus $\Gamma(T,R)$ is the ring of locally constant $\Lambda$-valued functions, with its pointwise ring operations.

source.place: Tag 099T (lemma-fully-faithful), applied to the finite constant coefficient sheaf; etale constant-module model of lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-locally-constant, made constant-label compatible using the cited sheafification criterion (local representatives: sites.tex Tag 00WK) and morphisms.tex Tag 02GP; blueprint Step 1 global sections

proof.text: By the global-sections rule of [def-pur-sheaf-hom], step 3 identifies $\operatorname{End}(L)$ with $\Gamma(T,R)$ by $r\mapsto(s\mapsto rs)$. This is a ring isomorphism, since $m_r\circ m_s=m_{rs}$ and $m_1=1_L$. If $m_r$ is invertible, its inverse has a unique scalar $s$ by the same isomorphism, and the two inverse equations give $rs=sr=1$. Conversely these equations make $m_s$ its inverse. A section of the sheaf $R^\times$ is precisely a section $r$ of $R$ equipped with an inverse: local inverses are unique, hence glue, so $\Gamma(T,R^\times)=\Gamma(T,R)^\times$. Under step 5 these are exactly locally constant functions with values in $\Lambda^\times$: pointwise inversion is locally constant on the same open fibers. This proves all of clause (1), including the uniqueness and the asserted automorphism group.

source.place: Proof Step 1: endomorphism ring, its units, and locally constant unit functions

proof.text: For two given isomorphisms $\varphi,\psi:L\to M$, set $b=\psi\circ\varphi^{-1}$. It is an automorphism of $M$. Apply clause (1), already proved, to $M$ to obtain its unique scalar unit $u$, so $b=m_u$ and $\psi=m_u\circ\varphi$. If $m_{u'}\circ\varphi=\psi$, composition with $\varphi^{-1}$ gives $m_{u'}=b$, hence $u'=u$. Finally, for a given isomorphism $\varphi$ and $v\in\Lambda^\times$, the constant section $v$ and its constant inverse define $m_v$ and $m_{v^{-1}}$, so $\psi=m_v\circ\varphi$ is an isomorphism. In the geometric-stalk colimit of [def-weil-proetale-geometric-stalk], restrictions are linear and multiplication by the constant label $v$ sends the class of any section $s$ to the class of $vs$. Therefore $\psi_{\bar t}=v\cdot\varphi_{\bar t}$. This asserts existence relative to the given $\varphi$; it does not assert that arbitrary $L$ and $M$ are isomorphic.
